title: Introduce contextual probe orchestrator and soft-fail drift attenuator
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: existing smoke/eval runners surface brittle regressions but often overload incident channels for transient drift. This PR adds a lightweight contextual probe orchestrator and a soft-fail drift attenuator to reduce noisy CI failures while preserving high-fidelity detection for sustained regressions. Summary of changes: 1) eval/probe/orchestrator.py: new orchestrator that schedules probes by semantic cohort, recency, and failure signal strength; supports priority preemption and late-arrival reconciliation; 2) eval/hooks/soft_fail_attenuator.py: attenuation policy that converts short-lived signal spikes into soft-fail alerts with gradual escalation; configurable per-prompt tolerance profiles and a time-windowed decay; 3) ci/eval_pipeline.yml: integrate a new orchestration stage with feature flags to toggle attenuation behavior, a new heartbeat metric and a failure-tier counter; 4) tests/*: unit + integration harness that simulates bursty drift, late-arriving examples, and recovery scenarios; 5) docs/eval/runbook.md: operational guidance and runbook for oncall. Checklist: - [x] Implementation with feature flag and default off for prod - [x] Unit tests for scheduling and soft-fail logic - [x] Integration smoke to exercise pipeline - [x] Metrics and dashboard glue - [x] Runbook and how-to disable/override behavior Migration notes: no breaking API changes; config shapes added under eval.probes.* and ci pipeline requires minor CI runner permission to emit new metrics. How to validate locally: run tests/probe_integration.py and flip feature flag locally (eval.features.contextual_probe = true) to reproduce prioritization. Related: ENG-6123 (probe prioritizer research), ENG-6180 (runbook/observability deliverable). Links: Linear/ENG-6123, Linear/ENG-6180. Rationale: many historical CI flakes were traced to transient upstream model churn or tokenization pipeline bumps; rather than immediate hard-gating, the attenuator creates a two-tier response so triage can focus on sustained regressions.
